A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same decoder-interpolation approach to continual open-vocabulary segmentation, renamed ConOVS in v2. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments with fc-clip and X-Decoder, baseline comparisons, component ablations, timing measurements, and qualitative results, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation experiments and adds original results on challenging domains, longer learning sequences, alternative training settings, component choices, and computational resources.

M1.justification: Both versions freeze encoders, fine-tune dataset-specific decoders, estimate image/text MVN log-likelihoods, apply softmax and element-wise maximum, and interpolate decoder weight differences. ConOVS, expert terminology, and the task-vector equation restate this procedure. The additional ablations and applicability discussion do not establish a change to the adopted method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on GTA5, DarkZurich, and FoggyZurich, covering synthetic, nighttime, and foggy driving conditions absent from v1's experiments. Scenario S4 also expands incremental training to BDD100K and Mapillary Vistas, which v1 used only for evaluation. The original segmentation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds retraining to the corresponding main benchmark comparisons, whereas v1 evaluated joint training primarily in its motivation analysis. Appendix G.6 adds an evaluated reimplementation of SemLA. OneFormer replaces Mask2Former as the introductory closed-set reference. ER, LwF, EWC, and ECLIPSE remain in the main continual-learning comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include separate seen/unseen-class evaluation on ADE20K, SQ/RQ diagnostics, ADE20K pre-training controls, a combined Cityscapes–ADE20K incremental dataset, training with 5% of Cityscapes, and retraining schedules from 10k to 100k iterations. These extend the evaluation design; newly disclosed settings do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds temperature sensitivity, encoder-versus-decoder adaptation, normalization and modality-fusion ablations, truly unseen-class analysis, resource scaling, and robustness checks for challenging domains, limited data, mixed domains, and longer sequences. Existing modality, prototype, prompt, and argmax analyses largely remain. v1's additional qualitative galleries in Figures A1–A3 are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed specifications, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's checklist item 7 explains that error bars are omitted because repeated trials would be costly, but introduces no uncertainty estimates or specified replication procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for the new comparisons and analyses, including unseen-class mIoU of 30.9 versus baseline 28.6 in Table 4a. Most matched legacy scores remain unchanged. However, the reported Cityscapes PQ delta after ADE20K adaptation changes from -0.3 in v1 Table 2b to +0.9 in v2 Table 1b; v2 Table A15 instead reports +0.8. The PDFs do not explain this discrepancy.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4 adds explicit definitions of the accumulated seen-class set and an unseen-class set disjoint from it, refining v1's dataset-level problem definition. The task-vector interpolation equation is mathematically equivalent to v1's update. Neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains adaptation to new data while preserving prior knowledge. v2 additionally presents the sequential-data scenario as a contribution and broadens its headline claim to consistent superiority over retraining and other methods across pre-training, incremental, and zero-shot datasets. This strengthens the comparative claim without replacing the underlying contribution.

C2.justification: v2 attributes zero-shot gains primarily to segmentation quality and acknowledges that sufficiently long retraining can outperform ConOVS on pre-training and incremental datasets, qualifying v1's joint-training discussion. It adds interpretations of component behavior, possible applications to detection and weak supervision, an extra-encoding cost for cost-based OVS, and bias preservation as a limitation. These proposed applications are not experimentally validated.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands technical disclosure through Appendices A, B, and D: two NVIDIA A5000 GPUs, ER sampling without duplicate images, LwF probability construction, EWC Fisher-estimation data, KDE bandwidth 0.5, training time and memory, inference-stage timings, and storage per dataset. These are largely newly documented details rather than demonstrated changes to existing implementations.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion shifts from general fine-tuning and forgetting toward continual learning with open label spaces and mixture-of-experts approaches. v2 adds relevant open-vocabulary continual-learning literature and explicitly positions ConOVS against SemLA, identifying differences in modalities, domain modeling, and adapted components. Much of v1's general fine-tuning bibliography is replaced.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, motivation, methodology, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Motivation becomes a separate section; comparison-method descriptions and qualitative discussion move to organized appendices A–J. Terminology changes to pre-training, incremental, and zero-shot datasets, alongside a new title, author information, broader-impact discussion, and checklist.

P2.justification: v2 introduces prominent bar, radar, and scatter summaries and numerous new tables, adds columns to retained comparisons, and combines the interpolation histograms and schematic into Figure 4. v1 Figures 5 and 8 reappear as Figures C1 and I3, with revised presentation; the additional qualitative galleries disappear. The document also adopts a substantially different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by separating truly unseen classes, testing difficult domains and limited data, comparing against SemLA, and examining whether longer retraining reverses the apparent advantage. These address important evidential gaps in v1, while implementation and resource disclosures improve transparency. The gains outweigh remaining problems, including inconsistent S2 PQ reporting and overbroad superiority claims: Table 3, for example, favors retraining on PAS-21.
